text: “The Jazz Singer” opens — the talkies are here! Audiences stream into the theaters. Silent-film veterans fear for their voices.
Stock market crash on Wall Street. Studio budgets collapse, fees come under pressure.
The Hays Code is enforced. Scandals are now more dangerous than ever.
War in Europe. The foreign markets fall away.
Post-war boom! Never before have so many Americans gone to the movies.
The Paramount decree smashes the studio system — and television conquers the living rooms.
CinemaScope! Widescreen is meant to win audiences back from the TV set.
“Bonnie and Clyde” shocks and thrills: New Hollywood begins. Young character actors are in demand.
“Jaws” invents the blockbuster. Summer now belongs to the movies.
“Star Wars” shatters every record. Franchise potential becomes a currency.
“The Matrix” and the DVD business: Hollywood is swimming in money.
A writers' strike paralyzes Hollywood — and a mail-order company called Netflix starts streaming.
Streaming boom and the superhero era: content is king.
Pandemic. Theaters close worldwide. Productions are on ice.
The theaters reopen — but the audience returns only hesitantly.
